Moses Coker
Preserved Primary Document • coker-m2.htm
Moses was mentioned in the
1867
will of his grandfather's brother,  Moses Coker  of Caroline Co., MD. He received a bequest of $200 which was one of the largest bequests the senior Moses made.

Moses Coker

Preserved Primary Document • coker-m2.htm

Moses was mentioned in the 1867 will of his grandfather's brother, Moses Coker of Caroline Co., MD. He received a bequest of $200 which was one of the largest bequests the senior Moses made. Moses Coker, the younger, was a farmer in Kenton Hundred, DE most of his life. He and Mary Ann had 16 children, most of whom married within the mixed blood Delaware community: Selenar Coker (born 6 Aug. 1872- died before 1923) Mary Eliza Coker (born 13 Aug. 1873- died before 1923) married Cassius MOSLEY on 23 September, 1900 Robert James Coker (1874- died after 1957) married Nellie Miller Andrew Coker (born 28 March, 1876 - died before 1923) Lucinda Coker (born 15 Sept. 1877-died before 1923) Albeda Coker (1878-1953)married Cassius Mosley & Calvin Clark Sadie J. Coker (born 14 Jan. 1881- died 15 Dec. 1957)married William Washington Angie Bell Coker (1882- 1937) married Andrew Mosley John Clayton Coker (1884-1915) married Phoebe Carney Moses Elwood Coker (b. 15 Feb. 1886- 21 July, 1915) married Margaret MORGAN Catherine Coker (born 27 Feb. 1888- died before 1923) William H. Coker (1889-1965) married Lillie Mae Sammons Amanda E. Coker (1891-1963) married Clem Carney Daniel Coker (born 12 May, 1893- died before 1923) Nathan Louis Coker (born 5 Dec. 1894-died 1955) married Anna MOSLEY Caroline Coker (1896-1981) married Levin Jackson Moses Coker died on 25 April, 1898. His death certificate lists Kenton Hundred as his place of residence, "yellow" as his race , his age as 49 and the cause of death "consumption". He is buried next to his wife, Mary Ann, who died 21 November, 1923, in Immanuel Union (Manship) Church cemetary in Cheswold., DE
